title: When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment…
paragraphs: When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment…
The field is quiet. Two brothers stand before the Lord. Two offerings rest upon stone.
At first glance, both seem generous… both cost something. But as I watch, I sense it wasn’t the gift. It was the heart.

One offering rises with intentional surrender — first and best, given with reverence. The other feels measured… calculated… perhaps obligated. The difference is invisible to human eyes, yet unmistakable before God.
I stand there as a witness, not a biblical character, and I feel the weight of it. Worship is not about appearance. It is about wholehearted devotion.
And I wonder… when I bring my praise, my time, my service — is it my first and best? Or simply what remains?
What does wholehearted worship look like in my life today… and what might need to change?
